subtopics.title: PM's State Visit and Key Outcomes
subtopics.summary: The Prime Minister of India concluded a State Visit to Indonesia, reinforcing the India-Indonesia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. The visit brought the Prime Minister an Indonesian honour and several agreements covering defence, industry, health, disaster management and agriculture.
facts: Bintang Republik Indonesia Adipurna is Indonesia's highest civilian honour.
The Prime Minister was conferred the 35th Bintang Republik Indonesia Adipurna.
The Prime Minister is only the 2nd Indian PM to receive it, after Jawaharlal Nehru.
Indonesia signed a contract worth around USD 200 million for 2 batteries of BrahMos.
Indonesia placed its 1st international order for the indigenous Astra Beyond missile.
SAIL agreed to establish a Stainless Steel Slab Manufacturing Facility in Indonesia.
CDSCO and its Indonesian counterpart agreed to strengthen medical product regulation.
NDMA signed an MoU with Indonesia's Disaster Management Agency on preparedness and response.
India announced supply of 100 tonnes of high-quality wheat seeds (DWR-162).

subtopics.title: Strategic Partnership: Defence, Maritime and Digital
subtopics.summary: Indonesia occupies a pivotal position in India's Act East Policy, SAGAR vision and Indo-Pacific Strategy, close to the Strait of Malacca. Cooperation covers joint military exercises, maritime awareness, satellite support and digital commerce.
facts: Indonesia is India's 2nd largest trading partner within ASEAN.
Indonesia is the largest economy in ASEAN.
Major military exercises include IND-INDO CORPAT, Garuda Shakti, Samudra Shakti, Milan and Komodo.
A 3rd India-Indonesia Security Dialogue has been proposed to strengthen defence consultations.
India and Indonesia agreed to jointly develop Sabang Port, near the entrance to the Strait of Malacca.
Malacca is one of the world's busiest maritime chokepoints.
Indonesia will post a Liaison Officer at IFC-IOR to improve Maritime Domain Awareness.
ISRO and Indonesia's BRIN jointly operate the Biak Telemetry, Tracking and Command Facility.
Indonesia Open Network was inspired by India's Open Network for Digital Commerce model.

subtopics.title: Prambanan Temple and Shared Heritage
subtopics.summary: The Prambanan Temple Complex in Yogyakarta, locally known as Roro Jonggrang, is Indonesia's largest Hindu temple complex and India is supporting its conservation. Shared heritage and cultural diplomacy are reflected in the Tagore-Dewantara Year and a planned IIM Bangalore branch campus.
facts: Prambanan is locally known as Roro Jonggrang.
Prambanan is the largest Hindu temple complex in Indonesia.
Prambanan is the 2nd largest in Southeast Asia, after Angkor Wat in Cambodia.
It was built in the 9th and 10th centuries CE under the Sanjaya Dynasty (Mataram Kingdom).
It is dedicated to the Hindu Trinity of Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma.
British surveyor Colin Mackenzie formally rediscovered the ruins in 1811.
India will provide technical support for conservation of the Prambanan Temple Complex.
2026-27 is declared the Tagore-Dewantara Year of India-Indonesia Cultural and Educational Diplomacy.
The Tagore-Dewantara Year commemorates the centenary of Rabindranath Tagore's visit to Indonesia.
Approval was announced for an IIM Bangalore branch campus at Singhasari Special Economic Zone, East Java.
India presented a replica of the Nalanda Copper Plate to strengthen shared civilisational links.

subtopics.title: Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)
subtopics.summary: NAM is a group of states not formally aligned with or against any major power bloc, founded in 1961 in Belgrade, Serbia. It is rooted in the Ten Principles of the 1955 Bandung Conference, and India and Indonesia were both founding members.
facts: NAM is a group of states not formally aligned with or against any major power bloc.
NAM was founded in 1961 in Belgrade, Serbia.
NAM is based on the Ten Principles of the Bandung Conference, 1955.
Founding fathers include Jawaharlal Nehru (India), Sukarno (Indonesia), Josip Broz Tito (Yugoslavia) and Kwame Nkrumah (Ghana).
NAM emphasised the 4Ds: Detente, Disarmament, Decolonisation and Development of the Third World.
NAM contributed to the 1963 Partial Test Ban Treaty through declarations on nuclear testing and non-proliferation.
NAM helped create several nuclear-weapon-free zones.
NAM advocated for the Global South and supported anti-apartheid in South Africa and Namibia.
NAM has supported India's candidature at the UNSC.
NAM failed to halt the arms race and to resolve regional conflicts such as Iran-Pakistan and Russia-Ukraine.

quizzes.passage:
India's Prime Minister recently concluded a State Visit to Indonesia, an engagement that reinforced the India-Indonesia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. During the visit, the Prime Minister was conferred Indonesia's highest civilian honour, a recognition that marks a notable moment in bilateral ties.

The two countries share a history of cooperation on the world stage. Both played leading roles in the Bandung Conference of 1955, and both later became founding members of a group of states that are not formally aligned with any major power bloc. Their cooperation today spans several sectors. In defence, Indonesia agreed to procure an Indian supersonic cruise missile system. In maritime matters, the two countries agreed to develop a port near one of the world's busiest sea routes. Steel cooperation is also in place, with an Indian company agreeing to set up a manufacturing facility in Indonesia.

Cooperation extends to public health and disaster management as well. Regulators of the two countries agreed to strengthen cooperation on medical products, and the two governments signed a memorandum on preparedness and response. In agriculture, India announced a supply of high-quality wheat seeds to Indonesia. Taken together, these steps show how a bilateral partnership can combine defence, industry, health and food security.

quizzes.passage:
India and Indonesia describe their relationship as a comprehensive strategic partnership, and their cooperation now reaches into defence, digital systems and maritime awareness. Indonesia occupies a pivotal position in India's wider engagement with the region. Its place in India's Act East Policy and Indo-Pacific strategy gives the partnership strategic weight, and Indonesia's location matters because one of the world's busiest maritime chokepoints lies close by.

On defence, the two countries take part in several joint military exercises, and a further security dialogue has been proposed to strengthen defence consultations. Indonesia's role also extends to maritime surveillance. It will place a liaison officer at a regional maritime information centre hosted by India to improve maritime domain awareness.

Digital cooperation is another area. Indonesia has launched a digital commerce network modelled on an Indian system. In space, a tracking facility in Indonesia is jointly run by an Indian space agency and an Indonesian research body to support satellite and launch vehicle missions.

Trade and economic ties are significant as well. Indonesia is among India's leading partners within ASEAN, and its large economy gives it weight in the grouping. Together, these areas show how a bilateral relationship can combine strategy, technology and commerce.
